## TL;DR

Wired the Task drawer’s existing handoff wait reason and computed progress label into the rendered check progress detail. Added a component-level test that seeds a running handoff waiting on a self-check and asserts that the drawer displays the wait reason instead of the generic “starting…” text. Kept the close-out commit route fail-fast and retained the lockfile conflict hook’s existing refusal and bookkeeping queue behavior.

## Work and rationale

The drawer already had `handoffWaitingReason` and `statusProgressLabel` computed from live task check and handoff state. The defect was at the final rendering boundary: `ChecksProgressDisplay` generated its own detail string, which becomes empty for a handoff wait without a check progress record. The result was that the user saw a generic progress state even though the drawer had a specific reason available.

Added an optional `detailLine` prop to `ChecksProgressDisplay` and passed `statusProgressLabel` from `TaskDrawer.vue`. The progress display now uses this supplied detail when present, while retaining its existing fallback behavior for other callers. This keeps label selection in the drawer, where the handoff and task state are already combined, and keeps the reusable display responsible for rendering the chosen detail. The test mounts the real drawer with a running handoff status and checks the actual progress element text; it also asserts the stale “starting…” label is absent.

Reviewed the close-out `waitForCheckGate: false` path. It guards the optional “commit dirty worktree and continue” action within the close-out HTTP request. Its explicit fast-fail comment and returned retryable error make immediate refusal appropriate: waiting there could tie up the request behind a long-running check, while the caller can retry after the check releases the worktree. Kept the existing behavior.

Reviewed `core/lockfile-conflict.ts`, which enforces write exclusion at git command and commit-hook boundaries. The current design refuses conflicting source writes immediately and handles bookkeeping commits through its serialized queue. Converting those low-level git operations into bounded waits would alter command latency and queue ordering semantics for all protected writes. No evidence in this task indicates that this should change, so this path remains fail-fast/queued as designed.

## Approaches tried

First traced the existing label computation, the `ChecksProgressDisplay` drawer detail fallback, and the two check-gate write paths. Considered putting the wait reason into the drawer title, but the task calls for the progress line and the detail row is the appropriate existing slot. Considered making the close-out route wait, but it is an HTTP action whose caller receives an actionable retry result; the bounded wait API remains available to handoff callers that should wait. For lockfile conflicts, the refusal hook is lower-level and shared across git writes, so a wait there would silently change unrelated command behavior.

## Challenges and blockers

The relevant state was already computed but not carried through the component boundary, so the issue was easy to miss when looking only at handoff status derivation. The waiting fixture likewise seeds a handoff state without a live check run; this matters because the old progress display had no detail to render in that case. No blocker remains.

## Key learnings

A meaningful state label can exist in a parent component and still disappear when a reusable child recomputes its own fallback. An explicit optional display override lets the state-owning component provide context without coupling the generic check display to handoff internals. The check-gate paths also have distinct responsibilities: handoff can wait with a bound, while an interactive close-out endpoint can reject quickly and let the user retry, and the git hook enforces immediate write safety plus ordered bookkeeping handling.

## Review follow-up

The first managed screenshot exposed that the drawer fixture used the synthetic task key while the declared shot deep-linked the real task, and that the live status poll could then overwrite fixture state. Updated the fixture to seed the deep-linked drawer task with the server-shaped top-level `reason`, and added a capture-only guard that preserves this status during the fixture render. Added a focused helper test for the real task query, unrelated task IDs, and normal non-capture navigation. The component test also now seeds the handoff state through the mocked status endpoint, matching the drawer’s actual mount and polling lifecycle.
